 Goldman Sachs sees RBI raising repo rate to 6.25% by mid-2027, India growth slowing to 7.2%
 The investment bank expects inflation to rise to 5.7% in 2027, above market expectations, as higher food prices and persistent cost pressures prompt further monetary tightening. 
 Ishaan Gera 
 November 18, 2026 / 16:16 IST

 Goldman Sachs expects RBI to raise repo rate to 6.25 percent.
 Headline inflation is forecast to average 5.7 percent in 2027.
 India's GDP growth is projected to moderate to 7.2 percent.

 Goldman Sachs expects the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to raise the repo rate by another 75 basis points to 6.25 percent by the second quarter of 2027, as persistent inflationary pressures threaten to push consumer prices close to the central bank's upper tolerance limit.
 In its India 2027 Outlook report, the investment bank forecast headline inflation to average 5.7 percent in calendar year 2027, compared with an estimated 4.6 percent in 2026.
 Story continues below Advertisement 
 Remove Ad 
 The bank expects a 25-basis-point rate hike in December 2026, followed by another 50 basis points in the first half of 2027.
 The outlook comes even as India's economic growth is expected to remain relatively strong. Goldman Sachs forecasts GDP growth at 7.2 percent in 2027, moderating from an estimated 7.9 percent in 2026, as the impact of earlier tax cuts, fiscal support and monetary easing begins to fade.
 “Upside surprise to growth has taken us by surprise, including markets and policymakers. Fiscal and quasi-fiscal policy aided consumer part of economy which predates the conflict. Excise duty cuts, fertilizer subsidies and OMCs absorption have supported consumers,” said Shantanu Sengupta, chief India economist, Goldman Sachs.

 Inflation pressures broaden

 Food inflation is expected to be the principal driver of price pressures in 2027, with Goldman Sachs projecting an increase to 7.7 percent from 5.6 percent in 2026.
 Warmer winter temperatures and El Niño-related weather disruptions are likely to affect agricultural production, particularly pulses, cereals and sugar, the investment bank said.
 Story continues below Advertisement 
 Remove Ad 
 Goldman Sachs estimates that around 63 percent of India’s core goods basket recorded sequential annualised inflation momentum exceeding 6 percent in October.
 Core inflation is expected to average 4.7 percent in 2027, compared with 4.2 percent in 2026. 
Persistently elevated crude oil and refined-product prices could necessitate more aggressive monetary tightening than currently anticipated, the report noted.
 Consumption growth to slow 
 Private consumption growth is projected to moderate to 7 percent in 2027 from 7.4 percent in 2026, reflecting the fading benefits of personal income tax reductions and GST rate rationalisation. 
However, the global investment bank noted that proposed implementation of the Eighth Pay Commission could provide a boost to urban consumption towards the end of 2027.
 Cash transfers ahead of assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh and four other states, which together account for around 13 percent of India's GDP, could provide some near-term support to household spending.
 Private investment improves, public capex faces pressure 
 Goldman Sachs expects investment growth to moderate to 8.5 percent in 2027 from 11 percent in 2026, despite early indications of a recovery in private capital expenditure. 
Goldman Sachs expects the Centre to maintain its fiscal deficit target at 4.3 percent of GDP in FY28.
 The investment bank noted that previous pay commission revisions were accompanied by reductions in capital expenditure allocations, suggesting a similar trade-off could emerge in the coming fiscal year.
 Rupee weakness may have peaked 
 On the external front, Goldman Sachs expects the rupee's period of sharp underperformance to be largely over, supported by RBI intervention and an anticipated recovery in foreign capital inflows.
 The investment bank forecasts the rupee at 94, 95 and 96 against the US dollar over the next three, six and twelve months, respectively.
 Foreign portfolio flows could recover as geopolitical tensions ease and concerns about India's limited exposure to the global AI investment cycle moderate, it noted.
 India's current account deficit is projected to widen to 1.1 percent of GDP in 2027 from 0.9 percent in 2026.
 Goldman Sachs expects remittances to moderate to $148 billion in 2027 from a record $160 billion in 2026.
